Q: Deploying Django backend and React frontend completely free — production-ready options? A:

I can suggest PythonAnywhere to host your Django backend, there is a free limited plan : https://www.pythonanywhere.com/pricing/ (HTTPS is enabled by default)
You may have some limitation like the storage, and the fact that you need to keep the app active every three months, but for a portfolio project, it can be enough!

For the database, you can use sqlite if that's a simple db. But if you really want Postgres, I already used ElephantSQL. but I think there are better choices (take a look at this page : https://github.com/alexeyfv/awesome-free-postgres)

As for React, you can simply host it on GitHub and deploy with GH Pages. Here's a tutorial : https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/reactjs/deployment-of-react-application-using-github-pages/

Q: Where can I download the Remote Debugger for Visual Studio 2017 A:

Code from my Remote Debugging Easy:

  • 2026 x64: https://aka.ms/vs/RemoteTools.amd64ret.enu.exe

  • 2026 x86: https://aka.ms/vs/RemoteTools.x86ret.enu.exe

  • 2022 x64: https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/964531996/RemoteTools.amd64ret.enu.exe

  • 2022 x86: https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/964531996/RemoteTools.x86ret.enu.exe

  • 2019 x64: https://aka.ms/vs/16/release/RemoteTools.amd64ret.enu.exe

  • 2019 x86: https://aka.ms/vs/16/release/RemoteTools.x86ret.enu.exe

  • 2017 x64: https://aka.ms/vs/15/release/RemoteTools.amd64ret.enu.exe

  • 2017 x86: https://aka.ms/vs/15/release/RemoteTools.x86ret.enu.exe

  • 2015 x64: https://download.microsoft.com/download/E/7/A/E7AEA696-A4EB-48DD-BA4A-9BE41A402400/rtools_setup_x64.exe

  • 2015 x86: https://download.microsoft.com/download/E/7/A/E7AEA696-A4EB-48DD-BA4A-9BE41A402400/rtools_setup_x86.exe

If you have installed VS already, the remote debugger is under the installation directory -> Common7\IDE\Remote Debugger. This is the most appropriate option for if you want to debug, you want VS in the host machine and the target machine should have the remote tools for that version, so you can just copy/paste the rdb directory to the target machine.

Q: Flatten multindex column in a pipe in pandas A:

@mozway's solution is great; what i proffer is an alternative - collapse_levels from pyjanitor - I am a contributor to the library:

In [4]: df.collapse_levels(sep='_')
Out[4]:
   1_red  1_blue  2_red  2_blue
0     10      20     30      40
1     50      60     70      80

If the levels of the MultiIndex are named, you can control the final outcome via the glue parameter.

Q: Is there any difference between Rust and Pony on ownership model? A:

Not a big expert on either language but here's mu $0.02. In Pony object ownership is per acvtor. An actor can have multiple mutable references to the same object. The objects within each actor are garbage collected. In Rust, one cannot have multiple mutable references, and there is no need for garbage collection. So these things are not the same, although t6he philosophies are similar.
